name: bigbyte.cc

profile.reading:
123 Central is the name applied to a data center at 123 Central Avenue NW in downtown Albuquerque, New Mexico, operated by bigbyte.cc, a regional colocation and hybrid cloud provider. The building's street number and its marketing name are the same, a detail that suggests the company built its public identity for the facility directly around the address rather than a separate brand name, a common practice among smaller regional colocation operators without the marketing budget of national providers.

On its own website, bigbyte.cc describes the property as a fully hardened secure campus and positions the company as colo-neutral, meaning it does not require customers to use a single upstream network provider and instead offers what it calls complete network redundancy through multi-provider connectivity. The company's service list includes colocation, data center as a service, hybrid cloud enablement, audit and compliance support, disaster recovery and business continuity services, and build-to-suit space for customers with specific requirements, along with scalable office and co-working space, suggesting the building houses more than pure server infrastructure and functions partly as an operations center for tenant staff.

The company's own materials do not publish a total square footage figure, an IT power capacity in megawatts, a tier classification, industry certifications such as SOC or PCI attestations, or a history of the building itself, including when it was constructed or converted to data center use. bigbyte.cc instead directs prospective customers to call a listed phone number for detailed technical specifications, a sales approach typical of regional and privately held colocation operators that compete on service and local relationships rather than on a published specifications sheet aimed at self-service comparison shopping. Albuquerque itself has a modest but real colocation market, serving as a secondary hub along the interstate fiber routes connecting Phoenix, El Paso, and Denver, and a downtown facility positioned to serve New Mexico state government, the University of New Mexico, and contractors tied to Sandia and Los Alamos National Laboratories would be a plausible niche for a locally focused, compliance-oriented operator like bigbyte.cc. Nothing on the company's public site independently confirms that positioning, however, and 123 Central's detailed specifications remain, at this writing, whatever it is prospective customers learn only by contacting the company directly.
profile.research_note: bigbyte.cc's own site (bigbyte.cc) confirms the 123 Central Ave NW Albuquerque address and phone but publishes no IT capacity, sqft, or certification figures for the facility.

reading:
bigbyte.cc Corp is a small, privately held colocation and business continuity operator in downtown Albuquerque, describing itself as New Mexico's first and only fully woman-owned continuity campus and as WBENC certified since inception. Its mailing address is a post office box, but it publishes a physical location, 123 Central Avenue NW, Albuquerque 87102, and that is exactly the address on the registry's single facility row. The OpenStreetMap node behind that row was created on 10 June 2022 and carries the same street number, so this is not one of the stale or borrowed attributions that turn up elsewhere in this registry. It is the company's own building, named for its own address.

Where it sits matters more than any marketing claim. Central Avenue is historic US Route 66, and 123 Central Avenue NW is a three-storey building a block from the Alvarado Transportation Center and immediately beside the eight-storey AT&T building at 111 Third Street NW, which is downtown Albuquerque's main telephone exchange. That is the city's fibre corridor, and the independent record bears out what the position implies. PeeringDB carries the building as facility 8736 under bigbyte.cc Corp, and six networks record a presence there: Cogent Communications, Lobo Internet Services, the ABQIX route servers, Tilver Enterprises, HOOP7NETWORK and FONENET. ABQIX, the Albuquerque Internet Exchange, lists this building as its facility in a record created in October 2020 and shows twelve participating networks. For a single-site operator, hosting a metropolitan exchange point is the most substantive thing that can be said about it.

What is not established is any measure of the building's capacity. bigbyte publishes no IT load, no utility service size, no generator rating and no white space area. A three megawatt figure previously attached to this record came from a commercial data centre directory rather than from the operator or any permit, and it has been removed rather than repeated. The company's own material describes what it sells instead of what it runs: colocation and continuity services, a carrier-neutral posture that lets clients bring their own network and managed service providers, and flexible workspace running from a single cubicle to 15,000 contiguous square feet, with conference, training and event space and fibre and category 6 plant throughout the building.

The company's public record beyond colocation is genuine and local. It became a service provider under the FCC's Rural Health Care Program in August 2020, it was involved in the Pueblo of Jemez sovereign broadband rollout announced in March 2021, and it currently promotes ABQ-NET, presented as New Mexico's node of Qunnect's quantum network. One recurring marketing claim should be read with care. The company says New Mexico's grid is independent of the rest of the country, which is not how the interconnections are actually drawn, since New Mexico utilities operate within the Western Interconnection. The state does sit near the seam between the Western and Eastern interconnections, and that is the fact underneath the claim.
